study_name: Crooke et al. 2017 integrated safety analysis of platelet effects of 2'MOE ASOs in the Ionis integrated 2'MOE safety database (ISDB)
design: Retrospective integrated (pooled) safety analysis of a sponsor-held clinical safety database; includes a subject-level meta-analysis stratified by trial. Not itself a clinical trial.
phase: not_applicable (pools phase 1, phase 2 and phase 3 trials plus open-label extensions)
indication: Mixed: cardiovascular disease (APOB, APOCIII, LPA), diabetes/obesity (PTP1B, GCCR, GCGR, FGFR4, APOCIII), thrombosis (FXI), inflammation/autoimmune (CRP, TNFA), pancreatitis (APOCIII), plus healthy-volunteer phase 1 trials (Table 2)
population: Healthy volunteers and patients; ISDB holds 3,476 subjects across 59 trials. Route split 86% SC, 8% IV, 6% SC+IV. ~1,000 subjects treated >=3 months; ~800 subject-years total exposure.
n_enrolled_note: 3,476 total subjects in 59 trials (Supplementary Table S1 'Total' row; Table 1 'Total' row), of whom 2,618 were 2'MOE ASO-treated (Table 1 'ASO, n' Total). Abstract instead states 'over 2,600' and '2,638' - see notes.
n_analyzed_platelet_note: Varies by analysis stratum - DO NOT SUM. Broadest ASO-treated platelet-evaluable denominator reported anywhere in the paper is 2,368 (Table 3 panel B, <75 K/uL and <50 K/uL rows) with 777 placebo. See the constituent analysis-stratum records for each stratum's own denominator.
route: Systemic: subcutaneous (86% of subjects), intravenous infusion (8%), both (6%)
dose_regimen: Up to 624 mg/week (abstract). Dose categories used throughout the analysis: >0-75, >75-175, >175-275, >275-375, >375-475, >475 mg/week.
duration: Single weeks up to 4.6 years (longest exposure, mipomersen open-label extension)
platelet_endpoint_basis: Methods: 'Data collected from 52 completed, randomized, placebo-controlled, and open-label trials were analyzed.' Statistical analysis: 'Evaluated subjects were those who received at least one dose of study drug and had at least one postbaseline (BSLN) platelet count and were included in the analyses. ... BSLN was defined as the last value before the first dose.' Methods: 'In phase 1 trials, platelet counts were evaluated weekly. In phase 2 and phase 3 trials, platelet counts were assessed on average every 2 and 4 weeks, respectively.' [Crooke 2017, Materials and Methods / Statistical analysis]
verification_locus: Europe PMC full text XML for PMC5467133 (fetched 2026-09-30) plus Supplementary Data PDF (Supp_Data.pdf, 10 pp., retrieved from the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint for PMC5467133). PMID 28145801; PMCID PMC5467133; doi:10.1089/nat.2016.0650 (Crooke ST et al., Nucleic Acid Ther 2017;27(3):121-129)
notes: HEADLINE FOR TRIAL GRAIN: all 387 measurement rows in this cluster come from ONE publication and ONE pooled evidence unit. They are table CELLS (band x dose-group, or band x treatment-arm) of the integrated analysis, NOT separate studies. Underlying trial counts, stated by the source: the ISDB contains 59 trials for 16 distinct 2'MOE ASOs (Supplementary Data, Detailed Methods: '32 phase 1 (sixteen 2'MOE ASOs), 21 phase 2 (ten 2'MOE ASOs), and 6 phase 3 (one 2'MOE ASO) trials'; by design 43 RCT / 9 open-label / 4 drug-drug interaction / 3 other = 59, Supplementary Table S1). The MAIN analysis set is 52 trials (43 RCT + 9 OL; Supplementary Table S2 header '52 Trials'); a nested randomized placebo-controlled set is 42 trials (Supplementary Tables S5-S7); the 4 DDI crossover trials are analysed separately (Supplementary Tables S3, S4). The paper NOWHERE enumerates the 52 (or 59) constituent trials by registry id, protocol id or name. Supplementary Table S1 gives COUNTS only. Only 8 constituent trials are individually identifiable from the source's own citations and stated trial attributes, and one further trial is an inference - see the registered_trial records in this file. DEFECT IN SOURCE (denominator inconsistency for the headline 7 events): the same 7 subjects with confirmed platelet counts <100 K/uL are given three different denominators - 2,249 in the Results ('6/2,249 or 0.3%' plus one further subject), 2,368 in the Discussion ('Among 2,368 subjects treated with 2'MOE ASOs ... only 7 (0.3%)'), and 2,638 in the Abstract ('Only 7 of 2,638 (0.3%)'). Table 1's own column sum of ASO-treated subjects is 2,618, not 2,638, so the Abstract figure is not reproducible from any table in the paper and is most likely a transposition of 2,618. Use 2,249 (Table 3 panel A, normal-baseline evaluable) as the defensible denominator for the Table 3 panel A incidences. SCOPE EXCLUSIONS stated by the source: oncology trials were excluded ('the large majority of cancer patients were treated with a 2'MOE ASO in combination with cytotoxic agents and no trials were placebo controlled'); ATL1102 (Limmroth 2014, phase 2a relapsing-remitting MS) was explicitly EXCLUDED ('Because we do not have access to the primary data, data from this study are not included in our database') - the ~11% figure quoted for ATL1102 in the Discussion is secondary citation of a third-party publication and is NOT ISDB data. registry_id NOT_REGISTERED: a retrospective pooled database analysis is not a prospective clinical trial and has no trial registration; established by the Materials and Methods description of it as an analysis of already-completed trials ('All data were from completed trials or unblinded and completed interim lock data'). No registration was sought or expected for this analysis. Row TMSR108 is assigned here rather than to a narrower stratum: its locus sentence states a scope of 'all RCTs' but the curated row's own supporting detail enumerates 7 subjects of whom 2 came from an open-label extension trial, i.e. the evidence spans the RCT and the open-label strata, so no single stratum is correct.

verification_locus: Crooke 2017 Table 3 (all 72 cells), Table 5 (row ">10% incidence"), Supplementary Table S2 (row "Platelets, K/uL Mean (SD)"), Results section "Low incidence of clinically relevant decreases in platelets" 3rd paragraph. All 72 Table 3 row values and all 8 Table 5 row values were re-extracted from the Europe PMC full-text XML and matched the curated readout_value for every cell with zero mismatches.
notes: QC RESULT: the 72 Table 3 rows are exactly the 9 reported bands (panel A: LLN-100, <100-75, <75-50, <50-25, <25 K/uL; panel B: <0.7xBSLN, <0.5xBSLN, <75, <50 K/uL) x 8 columns (Placebo, ASO total, and six dose bands) = 72. Every value was independently re-extracted from the article XML and matched. This is direct proof that the dose-group rows in this cluster are CELLS OF A POOLED TABLE and not separate studies. Of the 52 constituent trials, 8 are individually identifiable and verified (NCT00607373, NCT00794664, NCT00706849, NCT00770146, NCT01475825, NCT00694109, NCT01713361, NCT00048321) and 1 further (NCT00477594) is an unconfirmed inference. The remaining >=43 are enumerated by the source only as counts, so no records were created for them. Exclusions applied within this stratum, per Table 3 footnote a: 'Data collected on and after protocol-specified procedures, for example, total knee arthroplasty and endotoxin bolus; from nonplacebo comparator groups, and trials based on a crossover design, for example, drug-drug interaction trials were excluded.' TMSR107 (3 of 47 subjects with a subnormal baseline reaching <75-50 K/uL) is a sub-population NOT covered by Table 3 panel A, which required a normal baseline; its denominator (47) is disjoint from the 2,249. Cross-check: Table 3 panel A reports 1 ASO subject <75-50 K/uL among normal-baseline subjects, and 1 + 3 = 4 matches Table 3 panel B's '<75 K/uL  4 (0.2)' for ASO total. The curated row is internally consistent with the source.

phase: phase 1 to phase 3 (pooled, randomized placebo-controlled only)
indication: Mixed (see parent record, Table 2)
population: 784 placebo and 1,915 2'MOE ASO-treated subjects (Supplementary Table S5)
n_enrolled_note: 2,699 subjects in the stratum (784 placebo + 1,915 ASO; Supplementary Table S5 'n' row, header 'Randomized Placebo-Controlled Dataset (42 Trials, Phase 1 to Phase 3)')
n_analyzed_platelet_note: ASO-treated: 1,877 (<0.7xBSLN / <0.5xBSLN rows), 1,878 (<LLN / <75 / <50 rows), 1,788 (normal-baseline band analysis); placebo 777 and 749 respectively (Supplementary Table S6). Meta-analysis denominators are smaller and comparison-specific (Supplementary Tables S8, S9: ASO n of 80, 173, 823, 150, 137 across the five placebo comparisons) and OVERLAP across comparisons - never sum them. Coagulation sub-analysis (Supplementary Table S12) denominators: APTT 1,002 ASO / 425 placebo; PT 888 ASO / 393 placebo.

dose_regimen: Dose categories >0-75, >75-175, >175-275, >275-375, >375-475, >475 mg/week vs placebo; meta-analysis restricted to multi-dose SC cohorts in a single dose category as randomized

platelet_endpoint_basis: Supplementary Table S6 title: 'Incidence of Confirmed Platelet Reductions in Randomized Placebo-Controlled Trials (42 Trials, Phase 1 to Phase 3)', footnote b: 'Number of subjects with normal BSLN platelet counts and with post-BSLN values.' Statistical analysis: 'The meta-analysis was limited to platelet values collected during the treatment period, defined as the period from first dose to last dose plus 10 days. The following endpoints were evaluated in the meta-analyses: percent change from BSLN using the last nonmissing platelet value in the treatment period and confirmed decrease >30% from BSLN.' [Crooke 2017, Statistical analysis; Supplementary Tables S6, S7]
verification_locus: Crooke 2017 Supplementary Data PDF: Table S5 (baseline platelets row), Table S6 (all 80 cells), Table S7 (treatment and follow-up period rows, both panels), Table S8, Table S9, Table S12 (all 24 cells). All 80 Supplementary Table S6 values and all 24 Supplementary Table S12 values were re-extracted from the supplementary PDF and matched the curated readout_value with zero mismatches; S7, S8, S9 values were checked individually and matched.
notes: QC RESULT: the 80 S6 rows are exactly its 10 bands x 8 columns and all values matched on re-extraction. The 32 S7 rows are its 2 panels x 2 periods (treatment, follow-up) x 8 columns - the 'Study period' row of S7 was correctly NOT duplicated here because it repeats S6. Again: cells of pooled tables, not studies. WHY 42 AND NOT 43: Supplementary Table S1 footnote a: 'One trial excluded from the phase 2 RCT data set (0 placebo, 2 active).' So 43 randomized placebo-controlled trials in the ISDB, 42 in this analysis set. The 24 Supplementary Table S12 rows are COAGULATION endpoints (APTT, PT), not platelet counts, and are folded into this record because they are an endpoint restriction of this same randomized placebo-controlled trial set rather than a different trial set. Their population is further restricted - Supplementary Table S12 footnote a: 'Subjects had to have received at least two doses of study drug. Incidence based on observations from the last measure collected 5 days or more after a dose and before the end of the treatment period (10 days post last dose). Data from the FXI ASO trials were excluded due to the known pharmacological effect on APTT.' Consequently NCT01713361 does not contribute to the S12 rows. Supplementary Tables S8 and S9 report a 'No. of trials' per comparison (12, 20, 27, 15, 14 for the placebo comparisons; 12, 12, 17, 10, 6 for the adjacent-dose comparisons) but never name the trials, and the source itself warns they are not the same trials across comparisons: 'The trials used in one comparison (eg, >0-75 mg/week vs. placebo) were unlikely to be the same in another comparison (eg, >75-175 mg/week vs. placebo). Therefore, comparison of the effects was indirect and must be interpreted with caution.' These counts must not be added together. Of the 42 constituent trials, 6 are individually identifiable and verified (the five mipomersen phase 3 RCTs NCT00607373, NCT00794664, NCT00706849, NCT00770146, NCT01475825, plus the ISIS 104838 phase 2 RA trial NCT00048321). The open-label extensions and the open-label FXI TKA trial are NOT in this stratum because it is restricted to randomized placebo-controlled trials.

verification_locus: Crooke 2017 Results, section 'No increase in clinically relevant platelet decreases with longer-term mipomersen treatment'; Supplementary Data, Detailed Methods ('6 phase 3 (one 2'MOE ASO) [2-7] trials') and Supplementary Table S1 phase 3 columns; supplementary reference list entries 2-7.
notes: THIS IS THE KEY ENUMERATION FINDING. The source declares a 7-study set ('four 6-month RCTs, one 1-year RCT, and two open-label extension studies'). Six of the seven ARE individually identifiable, because the Supplementary Data sentence '6 phase 3 (one 2'MOE ASO) [2-7] trials' attaches citations [2]-[7] to them, and those six supplementary references are: [2] Raal 2010 Lancet (PMID 20227758), [3] McGowan 2012 PLoS One (PMID 23152839), [4] Stein 2012 Circulation (PMID 23060426), [5] Thomas 2013 J Am Coll Cardiol (PMID 24013058), [6] Santos 2015 Eur Heart J (PMID 24366918, the open-label extension), [7] Ballantyne 2016 ATVB conference abstract (the 1-year trial). Each was resolved to a registry record via the ClinicalTrials.gov v2 API AREA[ReferencePMID] search and verified for compound and phase. Records were created for all six. The SEVENTH study (the second open-label extension) is NOT identified by the source. No record was invented for it; instead a low-confidence candidate record (NCT00477594 / 301012-CS17) is included and explicitly flagged as an inference, not a source assertion. Hence constituents_identifiable = 'partial'. ARITHMETIC CORROBORATION of the four 6-month RCTs: their ClinicalTrials.gov ACTUAL enrollments are 51 + 58 + 124 + 158 = 391, against the source's 390 for the 6-month phase 3 dataset (Table 6 column totals 112 + 278 = 390; Table 7 and Supplementary Tables S10, S11 all use 129 placebo + 261 mipomersen = 390). A one-subject difference is consistent with a single non-dosed or non-evaluable subject. This sum is of DISJOINT trials and is used only to corroborate the identification, not as a pooled denominator. Likewise Supplementary Table S1's phase 3 open-label row (1 trial, 143 subjects) matches NCT00694109's 144 ACTUAL enrollment minus one. IMPORTANT ASYMMETRY: although the declared dataset spans 7 studies, Table 4 tabulates only the 5 RCTs - the open-label extension contribution appears only in the 52-trial pool (Table 3) and in the narrative '...not a single incident of a confirmed platelet drop below 50 K/uL in subjects treated with mipomersen for as long as 4.6 years' and 'Two of these subjects were from an open-label extension trial with total 2'MOE ASO exposures of 1.0 and 4.4 years'. TMSR1388 is the 4.6-year claim and is therefore assigned at this 7-study level rather than to the 5-RCT Table 4 stratum.

Part 1 = open-label, single-arm Phase 2 (dose-finding/expansion); Part 2 = randomised 2:1, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicentre Phase 3. The registration also contains a vital-rate/QTc substudy and an extension phase. ClinicalTrials.gov design module for NCT02598661: allocation RANDOMIZED, intervention model PARALLEL, primary purpose TREATMENT, masking DOUBLE (participant, investigator); phases ['PHASE2','PHASE3']; arm groups are listed as 'Phase 2: Imetelstat Sodium', 'Phase 3: Imetelstat Sodium', 'Phase 3: Placebo', 'QTc Substudy: Imetelstat Sodium', 'QTc Substudy: Placebo', 'Extension Phase: Imetelstat Sodium', 'Extension Phase: Extended Follow-up'. The FDA review analyses the Phase 2 part, the Phase 3 part and a Phase 2+3 pool as three ANALYSIS GROUPINGS of this single trial; the Rytelo label reports only the Phase 3 part. All three groupings, plus the label statements derived from them, are deduplicated into this one trial record per hard rule 2.
compound: imetelstat (GRN163L; drug substance imetelstat sodium; US trade name Rytelo)
indication: transfusion-dependent IPSS low- or intermediate-1 risk (lower-risk) myelodysplastic syndrome, relapsed/refractory to or ineligible for erythropoiesis-stimulating agents; del(5q) and prior lenalidomide/HMA excluded
population: Adults with LR-MDS requiring >=4 RBC units over 8 weeks in the 16 weeks before randomisation, with ANC >=1.5 x10^9/L and PLATELETS >=75 x10^9/L at entry. Label section 14.1: 'Patients were ineligible if they had del(5q) cytogenetic abnormality or had received prior treatment with lenalidomide or hypomethylating agents.' Phase 3 safety population median age 72 (range 44-87), 77% >=65 y, 30% >=75 y, 60% male, 81% White. ENTRY-CRITERION CAVEAT carried from the source (FDA review printed p218): because entry required platelets >=75 x10^9/L, none of the platelet results generalise to patients starting below 75 x10^9/L.
n_enrolled_note: 289 (ClinicalTrials.gov actual enrolment for the whole registration, i.e. Phase 2 + Phase 3 + QTc substudy + extension). The regulatory analysis sets are smaller and must be used instead for any platelet denominator: Rytelo label section 14.1 'in 178 patients enrolled ... randomized in a 2:1 ratio to receive an intravenous infusion of RYTELO (n=118) 7.1 mg/kg or placebo (n=60)'; label section 6.1 safety population 'RYTELO (n=118) or placebo (n=59)' in 'a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial (IMerge) in 177 adult patients'. The FDA review's Phase 2 imetelstat analysis group is n=57.
n_analyzed_platelet_note: Phase 3: 118 imetelstat and 59 placebo (safety/laboratory analysis sets). Phase 2: 57 imetelstat. Phase 2 + Phase 3 pooled imetelstat: 175. These are the only platelet denominators used by the rows in this record; 175 = 118 + 57 and is a WITHIN-TRIAL pooling, not an extra population. Sub-denominators that appear inside individual rows: 77 (Phase 3 subjects who reached Grade 3/4 platelets, the denominator-at-risk for the bleeding-association analysis), 98 and 96 (Phase 3 subjects with evaluable aPTT and PT), 27 and 91 (Phase 3 imetelstat age subgroups <65 and >=65, which sum to 118), 51 (Phase 3 imetelstat subjects still contributing a platelet value at week 49-52), and ~17-19 (subjects with a value at cycle 13+). DISCREPANCY RESOLVED: review Table 97 prints the placebo denominator as N=60 while every other table uses N=59; the label shows why - 60 were randomised to placebo (section 14.1 efficacy population) but 59 received >=1 dose (section 6.1 safety population). Table 97 therefore uses the randomised set. Neither figure is an error; do not 'correct' the curated rows.
dose_regimen: 7.1 mg/kg every 4 weeks (28-day cycles) - this is the approved regimen and the dose expressed as imetelstat (free acid), as used throughout the FDA review, the Rytelo label and every curated row. UNIT-BASIS NOTE: the ClinicalTrials.gov record states a starting dose of 7.5 mg/kg because it expresses the dose as IMETELSTAT SODIUM ('Imetelstat sodium administered intravenously (IV), at a starting dose of 7.5 milligrams per kilogram (mg/kg), every 4 weeks'); 7.5 mg/kg imetelstat sodium and 7.1 mg/kg imetelstat are the registry and label renderings of the same administered amount, so the two numbers must not be treated as two dose levels. Label section 2.3 dose modifications: hold for platelets <50 x10^9/L, first reduction 5.6 mg/kg, second reduction 4.4 mg/kg q4w. The Phase 2 part permitted escalation (registry arm 'Phase 2: Imetelstat Sodium (Escalated to 9.4 mg/kg)', n=7 in the posted results).
duration: Treat until progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal. Label section 6.1: 'The median time on treatment with RYTELO was 8 months (range, 0 to 38 months); 69% of patients were exposed to RYTELO for 24 weeks or longer and 45% were exposed for 48 weeks or longer.' FDA review gives median 7.8 months on treatment for the Phase 3 imetelstat arm and median 32.29 weeks for the Phase 2 cohort. Platelet observation window is defined by the protocol monitoring schedule (see platelet_endpoint_basis) and the by-cycle analysis runs to cycle 13+.

notes:
MECHANISM FLAG (model eligibility): imetelstat is a 13-mer lipid(palmitoyl)-conjugated N3'->P5' THIO-PHOSPHORAMIDATE oligonucleotide that acts as a template antagonist of the RNA component of human telomerase (hTR), i.e. a competitive enzyme inhibitor, NOT a hybridisation-driven gene-silencing PS/2'-MOE antisense drug. Its thrombocytopenia is ON-TARGET MYELOSUPPRESSION: telomerase inhibition in haematopoietic (including megakaryocytic) progenitors of a diseased marrow, which is mechanistically distinct from the PS-backbone platelet effects (PF4-dependent / immune-mediated and acute non-immune platelet-binding mechanisms) that the PS-ASO rows in this dataset measure. Three internal lines of evidence support the on-target reading rather than a backbone/platelet-binding reading: (i) the cytopenia is pan-myeloid, not platelet-selective - at the recommended dose neutrophils 89%, leukocytes 92%, platelets 94% (FDA review Table 78); (ii) the dose-response is population-confounded by underlying marrow disease, the reviewer stating 'patients with MDS are more vulnerable to cytopenias compared to patients with solid tumors' (printed p284), which is a progenitor-reserve argument, not a chemistry argument; (iii) events are rapidly and repeatedly reversible on dose hold (median recovery 1.3 weeks) and recur on redosing (212 events in 77 patients), the kinetics of cyclical progenitor suppression. CONSEQUENCE: these rows must NOT be pooled with PS-ASO platelet rows for any sequence- or backbone-attribution model, and must not be used as a positive class member in a 'PS-backbone causes thrombocytopenia' classifier. They are legitimate for modality-breadth description and for dose/exposure-response methodology only.

SCOPE OF THIS RECORD: all 62 curated measurement rows that describe the MDS3001 Phase 2 cohort, the MDS3001 Phase 3 randomised comparison, the MDS3001 Phase 2+3 pool, the MDS3001-only exposure-response analyses, and the two Rytelo-label rows. They are one trial under hard rule 2. This is the ONLY unit in the imetelstat cluster for which patient-level platelet outcomes are reported at the study level.

WHY THE PHASE 2 AND PHASE 3 PARTS ARE NOT COUNTED AS TWO TRIALS: both are arms of registration NCT02598661 and appear as arm groups of one record ('Phase 2: Imetelstat Sodium', 'Phase 3: Imetelstat Sodium', 'Phase 3: Placebo'), with one EudraCT number and one sponsor protocol id. Counting them separately would double-count the registration. The cost of that choice is recorded here so a consumer can re-split if it needs cohort grain: the Phase 2 part is open-label and uncontrolled, the Phase 3 part is placebo-controlled, and the two have different platelet denominators (57 vs 118/59) and different results (e.g. Grade 3/4 thrombocytopenia 54.4% Phase 2 vs 61.9% Phase 3; serious thrombocytopenia 3.5% Phase 2 vs 0% Phase 3; discontinuation for thrombocytopenia 12.3% Phase 2 vs 3.4% Phase 3). Treating a Phase 2 row and a Phase 3 row as independent replications is defensible as internal replication but they are NOT independent trials.

LABEL ROWS DEDUPLICATED, NOT TYPED AS label_summary: TMSR690 and TMSR691 (source SRC-82B0FA, the Rytelo SPL) and TMSR648 (the FDA review's reproduction of the agreed section 5.1 text) are statements ABOUT this trial, not a separate unspecified label summary. The label itself says 'In the clinical trial' (singular) and section 6.1 names it: 'a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial (IMerge) in 177 adult patients'. The cell-for-cell match of the label's 48/31/33/24 by-cycle percentages to review Table 85 removes any doubt. Under hard rule 4 a label summary is typed separately only when the underlying population is unspecified; here it is specified, so hard rule 2 (deduplicate) governs.

UNRESOLVED NUMERIC DISCREPANCY, FLAGGED NOT FIXED (defect found in the underlying rows' source, not in the rows): TMSR648 carries 65.2% from the FDA review's Section 20 Labeling Recommendations table (printed p345, the text proposed/agreed at review time), whereas the APPROVED label as published states 65% (verified by fetching the SPL). 65.2% does not reconcile by ordinary rounding with any numerator/denominator pair printed elsewhere in the review - 77/118 is 65.25% which rounds to 65.3, and 65/8 percent figures in Tables 77 and 85 are printed to zero decimals. The exact numerator behind the 65.2% rendering is NOT printed anywhere in the sources held, so it is left as the source states it and NO arithmetic reconstruction is asserted. Both values are recorded_as_printed at their own loci and neither row was altered.

PART OF THE REGISTRATION NOT REPRESENTED BY ANY CURATED ROW: the vital-rate/QTc substudy. Its posted results carry their own thrombocytopenia counts (otherEvents 'Thrombocytopenia': QTc substudy imetelstat 25 of 35, QTc crossover imetelstat 9 of 14, QTc placebo 3 of 18) which appear in NO curated row and in no FDA review table used here. This is a known, bounded coverage gap in the cluster, recorded rather than silently filled. It also means the registration contains more imetelstat-exposed, platelet-monitored subjects than the 175 the dataset describes.

ROWS KEPT HERE THAT ARE NOT PLATELET-SPECIFIC: TMSR671 (aPTT prolonged 26% vs 17%) and TMSR672 (PT prolonged 34% vs 30%) are coagulation-time readouts the curator already flagged is_platelet_specific FALSE. They belong to this trial and are kept in its measurement_ids so the row inventory balances, but they must not be read as platelet endpoints. They are the one place where a classical sulfurised-oligonucleotide class effect could have shown itself, and the excess over placebo is small (+9 aPTT, +4 PT, one Grade 3-4 event per arm).

TWO ROWS CARRY readout_value 'TBD' BY DESIGN AND ARE STILL ASSIGNED HERE: TMSR641 (Figure 36 mean platelet trajectory) and TMSR642 (Figure 4 Grade 3/4 incidence by Cmax quartile). Both are plotted figures with no printed data table; the curator correctly refused to digitise them. They are assignable to this trial even though they carry no value, so they are NOT unassignable.

DOSE/EXPOSURE-RESPONSE EVIDENCE INSIDE THIS TRIAL (the scientifically load-bearing content): review Table 123 gives a significant positive exposure-response between Cycle 1 Cmax and Grade 3/4 thrombocytopenia in MDS3001 (pLRT 0.0192 univariate, 0.0195 multivariate) with AUC only a trend (0.0894/0.0594) and Cavg null (0.998); Table 124's final multiple logistic model retains Cmax (slope 0.0166 logit per ug/mL, 95% CI 0.00259-0.0317, p=0.0252) and BASELINE PLATELET COUNT (slope -0.00632, 95% CI -0.00952 to -0.00353, p=0.0000327), i.e. a low starting platelet count predicts severe thrombocytopenia MORE strongly than exposure does. The contrast the reviewer draws is important for mechanism: in the same trial no exposure metric predicted Grade 3/4 NEUTROPENIA (Cmax 0.145, AUC 0.827, Cavg 0.749), so within MDS3001 the exposure-driven cytopenia is specifically the platelet one even though the overall cytopenia pattern is pan-myeloid. FDA added the exposure statement to label section 12.2 and issued PMR #5 requiring a randomised trial of at least two dosages.

Any attribution of the 46.8% pooled figure purely to imetelstat should carry that caveat.

INDICATION CAVEAT THAT MATTERS EVEN MORE: constituent CP14B015 enrolled essential thrombocythemia and polycythemia vera patients, where the baseline platelet count is pathologically HIGH and platelet REDUCTION is the intended therapeutic effect, not a toxicity. Pooling an ET/PV cohort into a thrombocytopenia-toxicity incidence mixes an efficacy endpoint with a safety endpoint in opposite directions. Flagged explicitly so no model treats ET/PV platelet lowering as drug-induced thrombocytopenia.

With 13 of 391 patients the quantitative effect on the pooled 46.8% is small, but the label 'monotherapy' is not fully accurate for this constituent.

MECHANISM FLAG (model eligibility): imetelstat is a 13-mer lipid(palmitoyl)-conjugated N3'->P5' THIO-PHOSPHORAMIDATE oligonucleotide that acts as a template antagonist of the RNA component of human telomerase (hTR), i.e. a competitive enzyme inhibitor, NOT a hybridisation-driven gene-silencing PS/2'-MOE antisense drug. Its thrombocytopenia is ON-TARGET MYELOSUPPRESSION: telomerase inhibition in haematopoietic (including megakaryocytic) progenitors of a diseased marrow, which is mechanistically distinct from the PS-backbone platelet effects (PF4-dependent / immune-mediated and acute non-immune platelet-binding mechanisms) that the PS-ASO rows in this dataset measure. Three internal lines of evidence support the on-target reading rather than a backbone/platelet-binding reading: (i) the cytopenia is pan-myeloid, not platelet-selective - at the recommended dose neutrophils 89%, leukocytes 92%, platelets 94% (FDA review Table 78); (ii) the dose-response is population-confounded by underlying marrow disease, the reviewer stating 'patients with MDS are more vulnerable to cytopenias compared to patients with solid tumors' (printed p284), which is a progenitor-reserve argument, not a chemistry argument; (iii) events are rapidly and repeatedly reversible on dose hold (median recovery 1.3 weeks) and recur on redosing (212 events in 77 patients), the kinetics of cyclical progenitor suppression. CONSEQUENCE: these rows must NOT be pooled with PS-ASO platelet rows for any sequence- or backbone-attribution model, and must not be used as a positive class member in a 'PS-backbone causes thrombocytopenia' classifier. They are legitimate for modality-breadth description and for dose/exposure-response methodology only.

study_name: Crooke et al. 2016 - Integrated Safety Assessment of 2'-O-Methoxyethyl Chimeric Antisense Oligonucleotides in NonHuman Primates and Healthy Human Volunteers (human volunteer arm)
design: retrospective integrated (class-level) safety analysis drawing on a sponsor-built integrated safety database; the human component pools 15 randomised, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging phase 1 studies in healthy volunteers covering 12 unique 2'MOE chimeric ASOs. Results are reported by pooled weekly-dose band, not by study or by compound. (The companion non-human-primate dataset in the same paper is out of scope for this human-grain registry.)
compound: 2'-O-methoxyethyl (2'MOE) chimeric antisense oligonucleotide class pool - 12 unique ASOs, identified in the source only by molecular target (Supplementary Table S1)
indication: not applicable - healthy volunteers
population: 750 healthy human subjects (179 women, 571 men), 84.4% white, age 18-70 (mean 41.3 +/- 13.0), mean BMI 26.0 +/- 3.3
n_enrolled_note: 750 healthy volunteers across 15 randomised placebo-controlled studies (source: "The clinical study population of healthy volunteers was comprised of 750 human subjects" and "Treatment periods for the respective randomized placebo-controlled studies (n = 15) in healthy human volunteers ranged up to 6 weeks")
n_analyzed_platelet_note: 733 in the Table 2 platelet-threshold analysis - the sum of the printed, non-overlapping per-band denominators (placebo 184; active bands 122, 113, 175, 43, 78, 18); the paper does not print this total. The Supplementary Table S6b mean-platelet analysis uses a smaller set, because a cell was only reported where it contained at least 10 subjects and at least 4 ASOs (per-band n 25-65 at Dose 6, and the >275-375 mg and >475 mg bands are absent from it entirely).
route: subcutaneous and intravenous systemic dosing (pooled; the paper reports by weekly dose in mg, not by route)
dose_regimen: pooled dose bands up to >475 mg per week; multidose regimens gave study drug every other day in week 1, with or without weekly dosing thereafter (Supplementary Figure S2); mean results are indexed by dose number (Dose 1-6) rather than by calendar time
duration: up to 6 weeks of treatment; the over-time analysis included study data up to 10 days after the last dose
platelet_endpoint_basis: "in human studies, we observed no remarkable reduction in platelet counts over the course of treatment (Figure 4b) and no apparent dose or total exposure relationship (see Supplementary Table S6). The only incidence of platelet counts below 75,000 per microlitre occurred in a placebo treated subject (Table 2)." [Mol Ther 2016;24:1771-1782, Discussion; PMC5112040]. The endpoint was assessed under defined thresholds with a confirmation rule: Table 2 reports platelet counts below 75 K/mm3 by dose band on confirmed test results, and Supplementary Table S6b reports mean (SE), median, quartiles and min-max platelet counts by dose band at each dose number against a stated human LLN of 140 K/mm3 (Figure 4 legend).
verification_locus: Europe PMC EXT_ID:27357629 -> Mol Ther 2016;24:1771-1782, doi 10.1038/mt.2016.136, PMC5112040, Crooke ST et al. Full text XML fetched from Europe PMC on 2026-09-30; constituent-study count verified verbatim in the Results ("Safety laboratory tests"): "Treatment periods for the respective randomized placebo-controlled studies (n = 15) in healthy human volunteers ranged up to 6 weeks"; population verified in the Results opening: "comprised of 750 human subjects".
notes: NOT A TRIAL (hard rule 3), and OUT OF COMPOUND for this cluster - it carries no volanesorsen data; it sits in cluster_volanesorsen only because its Discussion cross-references the volanesorsen and IONIS-TTRRx phase 3 signals (those three rows are listed as unassignable). 15 constituent phase 1 trials are STATED but NOT individually identifiable: the source names no trial, protocol number or registry identifier, and identifies the 12 ASOs only by molecular target in Supplementary Table S1, so no constituent trial records were created (hard rule 3) and no registry ids were asserted (hard rule 1). CROSS-CLUSTER OVERLAP WARNING: this is one of a family of integrated analyses drawn from the same Ionis integrated safety database; a sibling analysis is curated in cluster_crooke2017_pooled (PMID 28145801 / doi 10.1089/nat.2016.0650) and another in this file (crooke2019-galnac3-integrated-hv). Subject-level overlap between these pools is likely, so their denominators must never be summed and they must not be counted as independent trials. SCIENTIFIC POINT this unit exists to carry: the only platelet count below 75,000/microlitre in 750 healthy volunteers occurred on placebo, while the >375-475 mg band showed a statistically significant mean decrement (207.4 vs 231.1 K/mm3, p<0.001) whose group minimum (147.0) still sat above the stated LLN - the paper's animal-to-human translation argument.

population: healthy volunteers in 8 phase 1 HV randomised controlled trials, one per ASO (Table 1 gives placebo/active/total per study: 18/49/67, 13/45/58, 12/42/54, 12/36/48, 14/42/56, 8/24/32, 12/29/41, 9/27/36)
n_enrolled_note: 392 total across the 8 phase 1 HV-RCTs (98 placebo, 294 active; Table 1 "Total" row). The primary integrated analyses exclude ISIS 721744 (KLKB1, n=32) per Table 1 footnote b ("Data not included in primary integrated analyses"), leaving 360 subjects (90 placebo, 270 active).
n_analyzed_platelet_note: 157 for the weekly multidose platelet analysis: Table 5 is titled "Incidence of Abnormal Laboratory Test Results in Weekly Multidose Regimen Cohort (N = 157)" and its Platelets row carries n = 36 placebo and 121 Total ASO, with dose-band n of 32, 38, 33, 12 and 6. The single-dose cohort is analysed separately (Supplementary Table S9 and Supplementary Figure S5) and its denominators were not captured in the curated rows; the two cohorts are different subjects and must not be summed.
dose_regimen: single ascending SC doses, and weekly multidose regimens pooled into bands >0-10, >10-20, >20-40, >40-60 and >60 mg/week (4-8 SC doses over up to 6 weeks); GalNAc3 conjugation raises potency so the mg doses are roughly an order of magnitude below the unconjugated 2'MOE bands
duration: single dose, or 4-8 weekly SC doses over up to 6 weeks
platelet_endpoint_basis: "Table 5. Incidence of Abnormal Laboratory Test Results in Weekly Multidose Regimen Cohort (N = 157) ... Hematology | Platelets, n: 36 | 121 | 32 | 38 | 33 | 12 | 6; <100 K/mm3, n (%): 0 (0.0) ... ; <75 K/mm3, n (%): 0 (0.0) ..." [Nucleic Acid Ther 2019;29:16-32, Table 5; PMC6386089], supported by the Results text "As can be seen, there were no effects observed at any dose level on the mean values of any of the analytes measured (Figs. 5-7)" and by Supplementary Table S5 (mean, median, min-max platelets by dose number and dose band) and Supplementary Figure S5 (individual platelet trajectories, single-dose cohort). The zeros are therefore ASSESSED zeros against stated thresholds with printed denominators, not absence of reporting (hard rule 5).

notes: NOT A TRIAL (hard rule 3), and OUT OF COMPOUND for this cluster - no volanesorsen data; the ApoC3-L member (ISIS 678354) is olezarsen, volanesorsen's GalNAc3-conjugated successor, which is why the row set was clustered here. 8 constituent phase 1 HV-RCTs are enumerated at compound level WITH per-study denominators (Table 1), so constituents_identifiable is "partial" rather than "no"; but the source gives no registry identifier for any of them, so NO constituent trial records were created and no NCT ids were asserted (hard rules 1, 3 and 6). A probe of ClinicalTrials.gov on 2026-09-30 confirms that plausible phase 1 HV records exist for some of these compounds but cannot be matched 1:1 on the evidence available: e.g. NCT02414594 (IONIS-APO(a)-LRx, phase 1, healthy volunteers) lists enrolment 60 against Table 1's 58 for ISIS 681257, and NCT02709850 (IONIS-ANGPTL3-LRx, phase 1, healthy volunteers) lists 48 which matches Table 1's 48 for ISIS 703802 - one match and one mismatch is not a basis for asserting the mapping, so none is asserted. study_name: ORION-1 - A Placebo-controlled, Double-blind, Randomized Trial to Compare the Effect of Different Doses of ALN-PCSSC Given as Single or Multiple Subcutaneous Injections in Subjects With High Cardiovascular Risk and Elevated LDL-C (pre-specified platelet/immune safety analysis)
design: randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group phase 2 dose-ranging trial with single-dose and double-dose (day 1 and day 90) starting regimens; the platelet, immune-cell, immune-marker and anti-drug-antibody results curated here are the trial's PRE-SPECIFIED safety analysis, reported in a separate publication
indication: elevated LDL-C at high cardiovascular risk (atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, familial hypercholesterolaemia, diabetes)
population: 501 patients at high cardiovascular risk with elevated LDL-C across six inclisiran regimens and two placebo groups
n_enrolled_note: 501 (ClinicalTrials.gov actual enrolment, confirmed by the publication's 6068 analysed immunogenicity samples drawn from 501 patients and by the curated ADA row "1 of 501")
n_analyzed_platelet_note: 501 as entered into the pre-specified safety analysis, with group sizes stated verbatim: single dose 200 mg n=60, 300 mg n=62, 500 mg n=66; double dose 100 mg n=62, 200 mg n=63, 300 mg n=61; placebo single dose n=65, placebo double dose n=62 (60+62+66+62+63+61+65+62 = 501). Per-group day-180 completer counts are not printed, so the day-180 medians in Table 1 may rest on slightly smaller denominators.
dose_regimen: inclisiran 200, 300 or 500 mg SC once on day 1 (single-dose regimen), or 100, 200 or 300 mg SC on day 1 and day 90 (double-dose regimen); normal-saline placebo on the matching schedule
duration: 180 days for the platelet/haematology endpoints; up to 360 days for the longitudinal platelet and anti-drug-antibody follow-up
platelet_endpoint_basis: "At day 180, no significant alterations of platelet counts were observed in any of the dosing groups (change from baseline, SD: 200 mg: 0.8%; 300 mg: -0.5%; 500 mg: -1.8%; DD: 100 mg: 1.3%; 200 mg: -0.5%; 300 mg: 1.0%; no significant difference for any group as compared with placebo)." [Cardiovasc Res 2021;117:284-291, Abstract, "Methods and results"; the same values are tabulated in Table 1 "Changes of blood counts after 6-month treatment with Inclisiran", Platelets block, "Change median, %" row]. The analysis is pre-specified ("we present the pre-specified safety analysis from ORION-1 evaluating platelets, immune cells, immunological markers, antidrug antibodies"), so these are assessed negatives under a defined exposure and observation window, not absence of reporting (hard rule 5).
verification_locus: ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 record fetched 2026-09-30: https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT02597127 -> orgStudyIdInfo.id "MDCO-PCS-15-01", officialTitle "A Placebo-controlled, Double-blind, Randomized Trial to Compare the Effect of Different Doses of ALN-PCSSC Given as Single or Multiple Subcutaneous Injections in Subjects With High Cardiovascular Risk and Elevated LDL-C", PHASE2, enrolment 501 ACTUAL, sponsor The Medicines Company, intervention ALN-PCSSC (otherNames "PCSK9 synthesis inhibitor", "Inclisiran"), eight arms matching the publication exactly (200/300/500 mg bi-annual single dose, 100/200/300 mg quarterly double dose, saline on each schedule). Publication verified via Europe PMC EXT_ID:32243492 -> Landmesser U, Haghikia A, Leiter LA, Wright RS, Kallend D, Wijngaard P, Stoekenbroek R, Kastelein JJ, Ray KK, "Effect of inclisiran, the small-interfering RNA against proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9, on platelets, immune cells, and immunological biomarkers: a pre-specified analysis from ORION-1", Cardiovasc Res 2021;117:284-291, doi 10.1093/cvr/cvaa077; the abstract's six percent-change values match the six curated dose-group rows one-for-one.
notes: OUT OF COMPOUND for this cluster: inclisiran, not volanesorsen. It sits here because the same publication cross-cites the volanesorsen APPROACH and inotersen NEURO-TTR platelet findings as comparators. ONE TRIAL, not a pooled analysis: this is the pre-specified safety analysis of a single registered trial (hard rule 3 does not apply), so it is typed registered_trial and its 18 rows are dose-group cells of that one trial. CROSS-CLUSTER DEDUPLICATION WARNING: inclisiran also appears in cluster_other_regulatory via the Leqvio FDA NDA 214012 clinical review (SRC-C76E2B); if that review restates ORION-1 platelet data, those rows belong to THIS trial record (NCT02597127) and must not create a second inclisiran trial. The two TOLG258 rows from this same publication (TMSR1956, TMSR1957) are secondary citations of APPROACH and were assigned to volanesorsen-CS6, with the 45.5% discrepancy documented there.
